study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Loreto et al., Alzheimer's & Dementia: Diagnosis, Assessment & Disease Monitoring, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Alzheimer's disease heterogeneity revealed by neuroanatomical normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The reference cohort (n=33,072) was pooled from ABCD, Cam-CAN, CNP (UCLA-LA5c), FCON, HCP, OASIS3, PNC, TOP, and UKBB. An adaptation dataset (n=20) and the clinical cohort (n=86) were from Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust (SINGLE-SITE). Additionally, matched controls (n=79) from ADNI were used for case-control comparisons.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: The reference cohort consisted of a group of 33,072 cognitively normal adults pooled from publicly available neuroimaging datasets ... The adaptation dataset consisted of a group of 20 cognitively normal (CN) older adults who had an MRI scan at ICHT for research purposes ... the clinical cohort (n=86) ... CN individuals from the ADNI reference cohort (n=79)

answer.SINGLE-SITE: recalibration/adaptation for model-1 (n=20) and patient for clinical research (n=86)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The 33,072 reference cohort was used for pre-training the HBR model. The adaptation dataset of 20 CN was used for model calibration/optimization. The clinical cohort was used as the target for individual-level deviation analysis. ADNI controls were used for group-level comparison.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Hierarchical Bayesian regression was previously trained on the reference cohort ... This model was then optimized using cortical thickness data from controls scanned at the same acquisition site as the clinical cohort (n = 20) ... This recalibrated model was then used to generate regional cortical thickness z-scores for each participant in the clinical cohort ... Cortical thickness ... was compared between ... patients ... and CN individuals from the ADNI reference cohort (n = 79)
